title: lore agent context: always append the top-3 bundle-wide query hits not already selected; degrade to that section plus a warning when the profile is missing (OPAG-378 design ruling A)
description: DO NOT START until the binding record lands in opum-doc. opum-agent ruled Option A on 2026-09-24, relayed by cross-session message, and said the ruling binds once opum-doc records it; they are routing it there after opum-doc's recycle. Find the record there, read it, and implement against the record, not this description. Ruling as relayed: make the lore agent context pack query-augmented ALWAYS by adding the top-3 bundle-wide lore query hits not already selected, as id, title and snippet. When the profile is missing, degrade to that section plus a warning instead of exiting 3. Keep profiles. Rationale: the evidence is LCLI-573's measurement note (opum-doc b58accf, 69 tracker-derived questions). The implementation pack found the answer 8/69 times against 68/69 (title) or 51/69 (description prose) in query top-5; a miss cannot be detected from pack scores (hit 9.1-39.8, miss 5.4-38.1), so no fallback threshold exists. The change is additive and reversible. Code: src/core/agent-context.ts (candidates come only from profile.sources plus pinned, around :159-163; ranking via scoreBm25Records) and src/commands/agent.ts (the missing profile currently exits 3). The pack JSON envelope gains a field, so this is an additive contract change: check ADR-0005 and docs/reference/cli-contract.md.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The opum-doc record of the ruling is cited by commit and path before any code change
The pack carries a query-driven section of up to 3 bundle-wide hits not already selected (id, title, snippet), in both --json (an additive field) and --plain output
A missing profile yields that section plus a warning, not exit 3, if the record says so

Re-run the LCLI-573 measurement on opum-doc and report pack recall with the new section against the old pack, plus the byte cost. AMENDED 2026-09-24: the criterion first said "69-question", but the rule LCLI-573 recorded yields 88 questions from 247 records, and five other readings gave 63, 64 or 87, never 69. The baseline itself reproduces exactly (8 hits, same byte median and range), so the set is measured on the rule as recorded, not on an unrecoverable 69.

implementationNotes: BINDING RECORD LANDED, verified by ref on 2026-09-24: opum-doc docs/adr/make-lore-agent-context-always-query-augmented.md at origin/main 9222079 (ODOC-265, opum-ai/opum-doc#417). Its Decision section matches the ruling described here: top-3 not-yet-selected bundle-wide query hits as id/title/snippet (~1-1.5KB); a missing profile degrades to that section plus a warning instead of exit 3; profiles kept; additive envelope field; reversible. The 'do not start until recorded' gate is therefore lifted. Implement against the ADR text; this session did not start it, on the orchestrator's instruction (over budget).

AC4 MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-24. LCLI-573's method, on opum-doc b58accf (the baseline's own snapshot) and again on opum-doc main 9222079. Both trees were fetched by ref as GitHub tarballs into scratch space; opum-doc's working tree was never touched. Three builds per question, all from source: BASELINE = lore-cli origin/dev 70a25b8, pre-change (positive control); NEW = this branch; NONE = this branch with a profile that does not exist. Question = record title; answer = any documentation-named non-index docs/*.md. RESULTS (b58accf, identical at 9222079): baseline pack 8/88; new pack-only (pinned+sections) 8/88, 0 baseline hits lost; queryHits alone 83/88; NEW PACK INCLUDING QUERY SECTION 87/88, recovering 79 of the baseline's 80 misses; degraded missing-profile pack 87/88. The only miss is ODOC-106. BYTES: query section median 937B (711-1098B), always 3 hits. Whole pack median 48,106B new vs 48,105.5B baseline, because the budget is fixed and the section displaces about 0.9KB of ranked evidence at no recall cost. Latency median 0.50s vs 0.47s. QUESTION-SET DISCREPANCY: under the rule as recorded ('every record whose documentation field names an existing non-index docs/*.md', 247 records read) this snapshot yields 88 questions, not 69. Five readings (any valid entry 88, first entry valid 87, all entries valid 87, exactly one entry 63, exactly one valid entry 64) and a concept-graph existence check did not reproduce 69. The baseline still reproduces: 8 pack hits, and pack bytes identical to LCLI-573's record (median 48,106B, range 47,872-48,243B). The new pack misses only 1 of the 88, so on ANY 69-record subset its recall is at least 68/69, against 8/69. AC4 is left unchecked for the dispatcher: the criterion names the 69-question set, and this measured an 88-question superset of it.

ADR vs CODE, points where the ADR text did not settle the implementation. (a) The ADR says 'every pack'. compileAgentContext also feeds the opum-agent-workflow/v1 projection (lore agent project, and context --contract), so those packs gain queryHits too, and their packDigest/contextDigest values change. The projection's inputRevisions still list only catalog source files, so a query-hit doc can change the digest without appearing in inputRevisions. That is a design question for opum-agent; the fix would be in src/core/agent-workflow.ts, which is outside this dispatch's scope. (b) The missing-profile degrade is applied to the default context path, bare and --workspace. The --contract binding seam still fails closed with OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_ABSENT, since its contract forbids invented fallback data; the ADR does not address contract mode. 'agent show <missing>' still exits 3. (c) Budget, which the ADR does not address: the section is reserved ahead of ranked evidence, shrinks below 3 only when the pins leave no room, and never causes the mandatory-pin budget failure. Measured pack-only recall is unchanged (8/88). (d) The ADR estimates the section at about 1-1.5KB; measured median is 937B (711-1098B). (e) The spec's rule that Lore never follows an unlisted neighbour still holds for quoted evidence, because the section is body-free (id, title, snippet, score). Documented in docs/specs/agent-profile-context-retrieval.md, docs/reference/cli-surface.md and docs/reference/cli-contract.md (the kind registry gains the agent.* kinds; queryHits is additive under section 7.1, and ADR-0005 needs no change).

CORRECTION to the ADR-vs-CODE note's closing clause 'ADR-0005 needs no change': that clause was about the queryHits field, which §7.1 permits without a schemaVersion bump, and it silently covered a second change it did not examine. The exit 3 -> 0 remap for 'agent context <unknown profile>' is NOT additive: cli-contract §7.2 names reassigning a semantic exit code a contract-level change, and §7.1 lists 'remapping an existing exit code' among the changes requiring a schemaVersion bump. The review of opum-ai/lore-cli#245 (finding S3) caught it. Now recorded honestly as cli-contract §5.6 (an amendment, the convention §5.5 set), citing opum-doc docs/adr/make-lore-agent-context-always-query-augmented.md at opum-doc main 9222079, decision 2, plus a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry. schemaVersion stays 1, and §5.6 records whether §7.1's bump applies as an OPEN question for the orchestrator rather than settling it: the ADR calls the change additive (decision 4) and does not address the bump rule. ADR-0005 itself (the decision record) is still unedited; the contract doc is where the codes live.

finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#245. The plain `lore agent context` pack now appends up to 3 bundle-wide query hits it had not already selected (id, title, snippet): recall 87/88 against 8/88, for about 0.9KB of the fixed budget. When the budget cuts hits, it says so explicitly (queryHitsOmitted, queryHitsSectionOmitted). A missing profile degrades to that section plus a warning, at exit 0 instead of 3. Per ODOC-265 Amendment 1 (opum-doc a8bb596): workflow and contract packs stay hit-free and byte-identical to 0.9.2, and agent.context.export moves to schemaVersion 2 through a new per-kind mechanism (kindSchemaVersions in help --json; ADR-0005 amended). Two adversarial reviews: the first found blockers B1/B2, both fixed and mutation-tested; the second found nothing blocking after 111 byte-comparison runs. CI: run 36009215595 on a3cb4f65 green, plus this closing commit's own PR run.
